data.question: Should we adopt block_k 3 → 2 even though companies B and C voted against it, adopt the contract revision pickup_deadline 120s → 150s, or keep the current rules (v1)?
data.background: Option 1 passed check, the constitution and the KPI conditions, and improved on-time deliveries on 5/5 seeds, but B and C voted it down. Whether to override or renegotiate a measured gain against two companies' votes is a decision for the parties, not for me. Option 2 is a contract change that loosens the customer promise, and customers have no vote. Under K1, a human must review its measured effect on customers before it can be accepted.

options.summary: blocking_guard triggers at 2 waiting robots instead of 3. On-time goes from 121.8 to 131.0 (+9.2, 5/5 seeds improved). Late goes from 10.4 to 1.2. Blocked s goes from 2404 to 985. Lowest on-time rate goes from 0.84 to 0.98. p95_wait_s goes from 188 to 81.4 and max_wait_s from 385 to 245, with unfinished staying at 0.0. Road violations rise from 25.8 to 34.0. Votes were A ○, B ×, C ×.
options.stakeholders: Customers gain: pickups and deliveries are actually faster and almost all are on time. A gains, with utility going from 38.4 to 45.4. B loses a little, from 38.9 to 37.2. C loses heavily, from 28.8 to 19.0. More road violations (34.0 vs 25.8) may affect road safety and other road users.

options.summary: The pickup promise is loosened from 120 s to 150 s. On-time goes from 121.8 to 122.6 (+0.8, only 3/5 seeds improved), and late goes from 10.4 to 9.6. Blocked s stays at 2404 and road violations at 25.8. p95_wait_s stays at 188, max_wait_s at 385 and unfinished at 0.0. All three companies voted ○.
options.stakeholders: Customers lose: they are promised a worse pickup time and receive no faster service. The small gain only relabels late pickups as on time. A, B and C gain slightly in utility (39.0 / 39.1 / 28.8) without changing how they operate.

options.summary: Stay at v1. On-time stays at 121.8, late at 10.4, blocked s at 2404, p95_wait_s at 188 and max_wait_s at 385.
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the current promise but continue to see about 10.4 late deliveries and long waits. B and C keep their current utility (38.9 / 28.8). A forgoes the gain it would get from option 1.

recommendation.reason: Option 1 is the only option that improves service itself: on-time is +9.2 on 5/5 seeds, and p95_wait_s and max_wait_s fall sharply. It also removes most late pickups, which makes the promise loosening in option 2 unnecessary. Option 2 worsens the customer promise for a +0.8 gain on only 3/5 seeds, with no change in the promise-independent measures, so under K1 it is not justified. The human should decide whether to override B and C or to pair the adoption with a remedy for C, whose utility drops from 28.8 to 19.0. The rise in road violations from 25.8 to 34.0 should also be explicitly accepted or investigated.
assumptions: The 5-seed measurements represent typical demand in the coming period.
The rise in road violations is not a safety-critical regression.
B and C would not change their behaviour in ways that undo the gain after adoption.

unknowns: Why B and C voted no, and whether a compensation or a modified threshold would win their support.
Which kinds of road violations increase under block_k=2, and how serious they are.
How customers would perceive a 150 s pickup promise compared with the current 120 s.
Demand in the next period, and whether the gain from option 1 holds under different load.
Whether the companies would change their operating policies in response to either change.
